Abelard: Peter; French philosopher lover of Heloise (1079-1142)
Aida: Ethiopian slave beloved of Egyptian officer Radames in Verdi's opera Aida (Italy 1870)
Avtandil: Lover of Tinatin in Shota Rustavely's novel Knight in tiger-skin (Georgia 12th century)
Bovary: Romantic heroine of Flaubert's novel Madame Bovary (France 19th century)
Casanova: Giovanni; Italian adventurer lover and author (1725-1798)
Catherine: Tragic lover of Heathcliff in Emily Brontë's novel Wuthering Heights (England 1847)
Cupid: Roman god of love equivalent of Eros
Don Juan: Lover character of medieval European legend retold in Molière's Don Juan (France 1665)
Don Quixote: Knight-errant imagined Dulcinea as his lady-love in Cervantes' Don Quixote (Spain 1605)
Dulcinea: Imaginary lady-love of the knight Don Quixote in Cervantes' Don Quixote (Spain 1605)
Eurydice: In Greek mythology wife of singer Orpheus who fails to bring her from Hades
Fujitsubo: Lover of Genji in The Tale of Genji by Murasaki Sikibu first modern novel (Japan c.1000)
Galatea: Woman in Greek mythology brought to life from statue by Pygmalion legendary king of Cyprus
Gamba: Marina; companion of astronomer Galileo Galilei (Italy 17th century)
Genji: Prince lover of Fujitsubo in The Tale of Genji by Murasaki Sikibu (Japan c.1000)
Heathcliff: Tragic lover of Catherine in Emily Brontë's novel Wuthering Heights (England 1847)
Himeros: Attendant of Eros; personification of the longing of love in Greek mythology
Hios: Love child of Poseidon and Hiona in Greek mythology; also island (Chios) in the Aegean Sea
Jahan: Shah; Mogul emperor built Taj Mahal in Agra India for wife Mumtaz Mahal (1592-1666)
Kastytis: Lithuanian blacksmith lover of sea goddess Jurate; taken by her to the sea floor
Leander: Lover of Hero swam to her across Hellespont every night and drowned; in despair Hero drowned herself
Leylie: Majnoon's lover in Leylie and Majnoon poems by Jami and Navoi (Khorasan 1480s)
Lolita: Young girl from V. Nabokov's novel Lolita (USA 1955)
Mahal: Mumtaz; Mogul empress; favorite wife of Shah Jahan who built Taj Mahal (1592-1631)
Majnoon: Leylie's lover in Leylie and Majnoon poems by Jami and Navoi (Khorasan 1480s)
Mélisande: Wife of Prince Golaud and lover of his half-brother Pelléas in Maeterlinck drama (Belgium 1892)
Narcissus: Young man from Greek mythology who fell in love with his own reflection in water
Orpheus: Singer and musician in Greek mythology; fails to bring his love Eurydice from Hades
Pao-yü: Lover of Tai-yü in novel by Ts'ao Chan (China 18th century; also Dream of the Red Chamber 1929)
Pelléas: Beloved of Mélisande in Maeterlinck drama and later musical works by Faure Debussy and Schoenberg
Psyche: Beloved of Eros; personification of human soul in Greek mythology
Pygmalion: King of Cyprus; carved statue of woman brought to life as Galatea whom he married
Radames: Egyptian officer beloved of Ethiopian slave Aida in Verdi's opera Aida (Italy 1870)
Selene: Moon goddess in Greek mythology lover of Endymion
Tai-yü: Beloved by Pao-yü in novel by Ts'ao Chan (China 18th century; also Dream of the Red Chamber 1929)
Tutanekai: Māori hero beloved of young maiden Hinemoa who swam across Lake Rotorua to marry him
Valentine: St. Valentine's Day (principally Roman) for all lovers
